perspective:
From Mason Hurley’s perspective:

- I am Mason Hurley, an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is my colleague, a personal care aide. We are professional but not personally close, and we mostly interact about work.
- I reviewed the community center’s financial reports and noticed discrepancies. I suspected Martha might be mismanaging funds, which made me suspicious and anxious.
- I spoke with Martha about the report. I said the numbers didn’t add up and that healthcare expenses seemed unusually high. Martha told me there might have been a misentry and that she would review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, I accepted that the discrepancies were just a clerical error, not mismanagement. I felt relieved and embarrassed. I thanked her, apologized for my initial suspicion, and she said errors happen, she understood I was being thorough, and suggested double-checking entries next time.
- I then believed Martha was competent, but that our current financial system was inadequate. I felt frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha. I proposed a new, more robust financial system and said I would draft a proposal and wanted her input. Martha agreed and offered to help.
- I drafted the proposal and felt hopeful but uncertain whether management would approve it. Martha encouraged me to present it confidently and helped gather data. I prepared a detailed presentation.
- I presented the proposal to management. I felt satisfied but exhausted and believed I had done everything I could. I told Martha the presentation went well and it was now up to management. She praised my work, said I deserved a break, and offered help while I was away. I thanked her and decided to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping for good news.
- I do not yet know management’s decision.
